claims.text: The material begins as a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Brittle behavior is governed by competition among grain-boundary segregation, brittle grain-boundary precipitation, and rapid grain coarsening.
The compositionally complex nature of the alloy mitigates the processes responsible for brittle behavior.
Controlled variation of grain-boundary segregation can alter the proposed embrittlement response.
Controlled variation of brittle grain-boundary precipitation can alter the proposed embrittlement response.
Controlled variation of rapid grain coarsening can alter the proposed embrittlement response.
Grain-boundary structure and composition mediate the effect of the proposed processes on brittle behavior.
Brittle behavior emerges when grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation dominate.
Compositional complexity mitigates the embrittling effect of grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply under both high-temperature and low-temperature conditions.
Conventional alloys provide a baseline characterized by grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation.
The hypothesis would be falsified if grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation are shown not to be the primary mechanisms governing toughness degradation.
